scope: Days 31–60; canonical JSON, generator, deterministic specs and companion guides
conclusion: All 30 need a functional redesign before being presented as complete business automations. The existing renderer and deterministic calculations are useful building blocks. More nodes or longer notes alone do not establish a complete use case. Publication acceptance remains n8n’s decision.
existingStrengths: Typed validation and meaningful domain calculations
Credit quote and cap before paid submission
One accepted render followed by bounded polling
Completed media guard, retained URL and bounded preview
Real manual rendering and MP4 evidence for the existing generation paths
sharedDeficiencies: Every workflow uses the same manual sample/webhook-to-render graph.
No workflow fetches authoritative source records; upstream must prepare the whole video input.
No source-specific approval, stale event, cancellation or changed-record policy is implemented.
No persistent processed-record ledger or accepted-job recovery exists.
The current sourceKey is frequently a title/product/site/warehouse, not an immutable event-plus-revision deduplication key.
No mandatory destination, delivery result or source-system write-back completes the business need.
Business rules and instructions explicitly defer external messaging/publication to an extension.
The 18–24 second generic card videos sometimes omit source steps/details; they must link and retain the full authoritative record.
Existing successful manual runs prove rendering, not the proposed business source, state or delivery behavior.
nonPaddingAcceptanceGate: A named user with a specific recurring problem and a reason a brief video helps.
A configured production trigger and an implemented source acquisition path, not only hardcoded samples.
A domain-specific eligibility/approval branch and at least one meaningful zero-work or review path.
Enrichment/calculation from real source records that materially affects the result.
Persistent state keyed by source identity, revision and destination, with the accepted render job saved before waiting.
A delivered business artifact and recorded outcome; retry delivery from the saved completed job instead of rendering again.
Manual Docker evidence for success, duplicates, changed inputs, no-work/review, and a failed-delivery resume.
Setup and submission prose accurately describes all required integrations and the actual limits; it does not promise acceptance.

stateRequirements.identity: Use stable upstream record/event IDs plus revision or a deterministic content fingerprint. Do not use a display title as the only key.
stateRequirements.concurrency: A check-then-insert flow alone can race. Use an atomic unique claim or a serialized dispatcher. Do not claim exactly-once protection if the chosen storage cannot enforce it.
stateRequirements.manualTestCaveat: Workflow static data is not a substitute for demonstrated persistent manual-run state. Test the actual storage behavior in Docker.
stateRequirements.retryPolicy: Retry safe reads and delivery according to service semantics; never automatically resubmit a known accepted paid job. A timeout must retain the accepted job and route to recovery.

feasibleBuildStrategy: Keep the proven native Zvid render module. Implement source-specific queue/joins and outcomes around it. Google Sheets can supply many operations registers with one reusable credential and isolated test workbook; GitHub, Shopify, Form or authenticated source webhooks can supply event-driven records. Use native nodes when supported. An authenticated local source/sink contract can test an unavailable service adapter, but label that as a contract test rather than claiming the external integration was verified.
